data_status: STRICT MODE: this dataset contains only values that were compared with, or ingested directly from, retrieved sources: JPL (SSD, SBDB), NASA (NSSDC fact sheets and mission catalog, Small Spacecraft SoA report 2026, SLS page, Apollo 11 press kit, NTRS papers, ), ULA, ESA, NIST, and the Launch Library 2 aggregator. Records carry source_authority/confidence where the source is an aggregator or vendor-reported compilation. Recalled, estimated and fictional values (optimizer catalog, costs, engine/vehicle specs without a retrievable source, the user-supplied SpaceX table) are not included. Derived values are computed only from verified inputs and are labelled derived.

record.name: X-ray Spectrometer (XRS)
record.description: The MESSENGER X-Ray Spectrometer (XRS) will detect the K-flourescence X-ray emissions diagnostic of elements (Mg, Al, S, Ca, Ti, and Fe) within 1 mm of the surface. Surface abundances will be mapped with spatial resolutions down to 20 km. The primary objectives of this experiment are to help characterize the chemical composition and geologic history of Mercury. A total data return of about 1.5 Gb is expected. The XRS is an improved version of the design used on the NEAR-Shoemaker spacecraft. Mounted on the nadir facing instrument deck of MESSENGER, it consists of three cylindrical gas filled proportional counters, each 10 square cm, behind a 25 micrometer Be window. Each counter has a set of anti-coincidence wires to catch penetrating cosmic ray events, an internal Be liner to block x-rays produced by cosmic rays in the detector tube walls, and a 12 degree field of view Be-CU honeycomb collimator. Thin absorption filters (8.5 micrometer Mg and 8.5 micrometer Al) on two of the detectors separate the lower energy x-ray lines (Al, Mg, and Si). Energy spectra from 0.7 to 10 keV with a resolution (full width half maximum) of 350 eV are accumulated. The maximum input rate is 20 kHz and the integration period is 100 s at periapsis and 2000 s at apoapsis. A small (0.1 square mm) sunward pointing Si-PIN X-ray detector with a thin Be foil cover is mounted on the sunshade to measure the time-variable solar flux input to the planet.
